creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Nothing on a sidebar pane row says which machine the pane is on. The label is the directory and the harness (`lore · claude`), which reads the same for a laptop pane and a devenv pane, and with both machines attached to every window since 2026-09-08 (the two-home workaround is retired) the two are indistinguishable at a glance. The machine appears only as a heading row when it is unreachable or holds nothing (`roster.machines where machine.worthDrawing`), which is the one case with no panes to label. `Row.showsMachine` is set to `roster.spansMachines` on every pane row, and no view reads it: every reference in `Sources/` is an assignment. The CLI does better: `muster window` appends `(local)` or `(devenv)` to each row when the window spans machines.

Asked for 2026-09-08 after driving two windows from one home: "there's no great sidebar way to see which panes are laptop or devenv, there should be some visual redesign to make that clear."

## Directions

- A per-machine mark on the row that reads without a word: a colour swatch or glyph per daemon, assigned in config order and stable for the session, with the machine heading carrying the same mark so the sidebar is its own legend.
- Or grouping: tabs sectioned under a machine heading whenever the window spans machines, so position says it. This costs the single ordered tab list the numbered chords count along, so the mark is the cheaper first step.
- A cross-machine tab (`a_2IoXIHzri`) is why a section per machine cannot be the whole answer: one tab can hold panes from both, and there the mark has to sit on the pane row.

## Validating a fix

- Two windows with laptop and devenv panes listed in both: which machine a row is on is readable without reading its label, and the same mark identifies that machine in every window and on its heading row.
title: 🏷️ Nothing in the sidebar says which machine a pane is on
